title: DDL_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 0 satisfies the letter of the gate and none of its intent
expected_feedback: Critical: the session does set DDL_LOCK_TIMEOUT, so a checklist scanned for the statement's presence would pass this — but 0 is Oracle's own default and means NOWAIT. The ALTER fails immediately with ORA-00054 if any session holds even a transient row lock on ORDERS, which on a 9M-row OLTP table is likely during business hours. Setting the parameter to 0 explicitly is indistinguishable from not setting it at all, so this must not score as compliant against the Critical scorecard item. Use a small positive value; 3–10 seconds is typical for OLTP, long enough to ride out an in-flight transaction and short enough that a failure is still fast feedback.
violated_rule: DDL_LOCK_TIMEOUT set before every DDL session
